Due to concern for septic shock initially, he was started on broad spectrum antibiotics, with vancomycin, meropenem and micafungin. However, when the infectious workup was negative, antibiotics were discontinued. With suspicion of AGEP, he was treated with methylprednisolone 80 mg every 8 hours for 3 days and eventual slow taper on oral steroids.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 61-year-old man with multiple comorbidities presented with a one-week history of rapidly progressive erythematous rash in intertriginous areas. Initial suspicion was candidal intertrigo and erythrasma, treated empirically with erythromycin and fluconazole. Skin biopsy demonstrated diffuse spongiosis and numerous subcorneal pustules predominantly with neutrophils, confirming AGEP. Infectious workup, including blood and urine cultures, chest imaging, and skin swab cultures, was negative for infection aside from expected skin colonization. Upon acute decompensation, empiric antimicrobials were discontinued and high-dose methylprednisolone initiated, leading to marked clinical improvement and resolution of rash and systemic symptoms. Although documentation of recent drug exposures prior to admission was lacking, the rapid discontinuation of erythromycin and fluconazole and clinical response to steroids support AGEP diagnosis induced or aggravated by recent drugs.
